root_cause.text: The EROFS directory parser in `fs/erofs/dir.c` failed to validate trailing dirent `nameoff` values before using them in `strnlen(maxsize - nameoff)`, allowing `maxsize - nameoff` to underflow and causing out-of-bounds reads past the directory block.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that “the trailing dirents are special since the namelens are calculated with strnlen() with unchecked nameoffs” and that “nameoff >= maxsize, maxsize - nameoff can underflow, causing strnlen() to read past the directory block”; the patch adds `else if (maxsize <= nameoff) goto err_bogus;` before `strnlen()` and also tightens `de[0].nameoff` validation with `!nameoff || nameoff >= bsz || (nameoff % sizeof(*de))`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix EROFS directory entry parsing to detect invalid name offsets and lengths, including malformed non-trailing entries, and reject them as corrupted.
intent_record.what: The code changes directory entry name length calculation and validation in `erofs_fill_dentries()`: it replaces the `if (de + 1 >= end) ... else ...` logic with `if (de + 1 < end)` for non-trailing entries, adds an explicit `else if (maxsize <= nameoff) goto err_bogus;` check before calling `strnlen()` on the trailing entry, and replaces the corruption check `if (nameoff + de_namelen > maxsize || de_namelen > EROFS_NAME_LEN) { ... return -EFSCORRUPTED; }` with `if (!in_range32(de_namelen, 1, EROFS_NAME_LEN) || nameoff + de_namelen > maxsize) goto err_bogus;`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes malformed directory entries be rejected through the common bogus-entry error path when the name offset is out of bounds, when the computed name length is zero or otherwise outside the valid 1..EROFS_NAME_LEN range, or when the name would extend past the block size. It prevents invalid trailing entries from being processed and catches cases such as a negative length resulting from a bad next-entry offset.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle bogus directory entries in `erofs_fill_dentries()` by reporting filesystem corruption and returning `-EFSCORRUPTED`.
intent_record.what: An error label `err_bogus:` was added before the end of `erofs_fill_dentries()`, along with a call to `erofs_err(dir->i_sb, "bogus dirent @ nid %llu", EROFS_I(dir)->nid);`, a `DBG_BUGON(1);`, and a `return -EFSCORRUPTED;` instead of falling through to the existing `return 0;` path.
intent_record.how: This introduces an explicit corruption-handling path for invalid directory entries so that, when execution jumps to `err_bogus`, the filesystem logs the bad directory entry, triggers a debug assertion, and returns a corruption error rather than reporting success.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `erofs_readdir()` to validate `nameoff` more accurately by rejecting zero, out-of-range, and misaligned directory entry offsets.
intent_record.what: The validation condition for `nameoff` in `erofs_readdir()` was changed from `nameoff < sizeof(struct erofs_dirent) || nameoff >= bsz` to `!nameoff || nameoff >= bsz || (nameoff % sizeof(*de))`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, directory entries are now rejected not only when `nameoff` is zero or beyond the block size, but also when it is not aligned to the size of a directory entry structure. This tightens on-disk metadata validation and prevents processing malformed or corrupt directory entry layouts that could previously pass the old lower-bound check.

grouping_result.intent: Fix `erofs_readdir()` to validate `nameoff` more accurately by rejecting zero, out-of-range, and misaligned directory entry offsets.

consistency_review.core_intent: Harden EROFS directory entry parsing and readdir handling by validating directory entry offsets/lengths and rejecting malformed entries as filesystem corruption.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly harden EROFS directory parsing by validating dirent name offsets/lengths and rejecting malformed entries, which addresses the root cause of using invalid trailing `nameoff` values that could make `maxsize - nameoff` underflow and trigger out-of-bounds reads.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct vulnerable use: for the trailing dirent, it computes the length with maxsize - nameoff without first validating that nameoff is within bounds, so a too-large nameoff causes unsigned underflow and out-of-bounds read.
This pointer is derived from unvalidated nameoff before trailing-entry bounds checking, so an invalid nameoff can already move de_name outside the directory block and then be consumed by strnlen().

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement directly triggers the vulnerability: it uses maxsize - nameoff as the bound for strnlen() without first validating that nameoff is within maxsize. If nameoff is larger than maxsize for the trailing dirent, the subtraction underflows and strnlen() can read past the directory block.

This statement computes a name pointer from an unvalidated nameoff. When nameoff is out of bounds, de_name already points outside the directory block, and the subsequent strnlen() call dereferences it, contributing to the out-of-bounds read.

staging: erofs: keep corrupted fs from crashing kernel in erofs_readdir()

After commit 419d6efc50e9, kernel cannot be c
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the exact trailing-dirent handling and validation order. The vulnerable construct is present at lines 62-64: for the last dirent, `de_namelen = strnlen(de_name, maxsize - nameoff);` is computed before validating that `nameoff <= maxsize`. `nameoff` comes from on-disk data at line 59 (`nameoff = le16_to_cpu(de->nameoff);`) and is used immediately to form `de_name` at line 60. Only afterward does the code validate corruption at lines 68-73 with `if (unlikely(nameoff + de_namelen > maxsize || de_namelen > EROFS_NAME_LEN))`. This ordering matches the root cause: a corrupted trailing dirent with `nameoff > maxsize` makes `maxsize - nameoff` underflow, so `strnlen()` can read past the directory block before the later bounds check runs. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not yet in this function.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows both the directory entry parsing in `erofs_fill_dentries()` and the caller-side bounds setup in `erofs_readdir()`, which is the relevant logic for the described underflow/OOB read. The vulnerable construct is present in `erofs_fill_dentries()`: it reads `unsigned int nameoff = le16_to_cpu(de->nameoff);`, computes `const char *de_name = (char *)dentry_blk + nameoff;`, and then for the last dirent does `de_namelen = strnlen(de_name, maxsize - nameoff);`. There is no validation that `nameoff <= maxsize` before using `maxsize - nameoff`. Therefore, if a trailing dirent has a malformed `nameoff` larger than `maxsize`, the subtraction underflows and `strnlen()` is given an excessively large bound, matching the root cause. The code also lacks any guard for the initial block-wide `nameoff` argument beyond `nameoff = le16_to_cpu(de->nameoff); if (nameoff < sizeof(struct erofs_dirent) || nameoff >= bsz) ...`, which validates only the first dirent offset against block size, not each trailing dirent against `maxsize`. The fix is not present because there is no per-dirent check such as rejecting `nameoff > maxsize` before `strnlen(de_name, maxsize - nameoff)`.
